name: Twelve rational points with few ordinary lines
description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^9, not all collinear. Minimize the number of lines containing exactly two of the points (exact). Over the reals the minimum for 12 points is 6 and integer coordinates reach it, so the optimum is 6.

state_of_the_art.statement: The minimum is 6. Twelve points that are not all collinear determine at least 6 ordinary lines (OEIS A003034; the Kelly-Moser bound 3n/7 already gives 6), and a Böröczky configuration (six points of a conic and six points of a line) has a copy with integer coordinates and exactly 6 ordinary lines, which the package's tests verify with the evaluator.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Determine the minimum number of ordinary lines of n non-collinear points.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The Sylvester-Gallai and Dirac-Motzkin problems (Erdős Problem #210) are central in incidence geometry; the extremal Böröczky configurations come from regular polygons, and the 12-point one has a projective copy with rational coordinates.
